claim: mRNA is cotranscriptionally processed and packaged into messenger ribonucleoprotein particles (mRNPs) in the nucleus.
source: mRNA is cotranscrptionally processed and packaged into messenger ribonucleoprotein particles (mRNPs) in the nucleus.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about mRNA processing.

claim: Prior to export through the nuclear pore, mRNPs undergo several obligatory remodeling reactions.
source: Prior to export through the nuclear pore, mRNPs undergo several obligatory remodeling reactions.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about mRNP export.

claim: In yeast, one of the mRNP remodeling reactions involves loading of the mRNA-binding protein Yra1 by the DEAD-box ATPase Sub2 as assisted by the hetero-pentameric THO complex.
source: In yeast, one of these reactions involves loading of the mRNA-binding protein Yra1 by the DEAD-box ATPase Sub2 as assisted by the hetero-pentameric THO complex.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the TREX complex function in yeast.

claim: The crystal structure of a THO hetero-pentamer bound to Sub2 was determined at 6.0 Å resolution.
source: we determined crystal structures of two relevant complexes: a THO hetero-pentamer bound to Sub2 at 6.0 Å resolution
evidence: This is directly supported by the crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The crystal structure of Sub2 associated with an ATP analogue, RNA, and a C-terminal fragment of Yra1 (Yra1-C) was determined at 2.6 Å resolution.
source: we determined crystal structures of two relevant complexes: a THO hetero-pentamer bound to Sub2 at 6.0 Å resolution; and Sub2 associated with an ATP analogue, RNA, and a C-terminal fragment of Yra1 (Yra1-C) at 2.6 Å resolution.
evidence: This is directly supported by the crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The 25 nm long THO clamps Sub2 in a half-open configuration.
source: We found that the 25 nm long THO clamps Sub2 in a half-open configuration
evidence: This is supported by the structural data from the THO-Sub2 crystal structure.

claim: When bound to the ATP analogue, RNA and Yra1-C, Sub2 assumes a closed conformation.
source: in contrast, when bound to the ATP analogue, RNA and Yra1-C, Sub2 assumes a closed conformation.
evidence: This is supported by the structural data from the Sub2•Yra1-C•RNA crystal structure.

claim: THO stimulated Sub2's intrinsic ATPase activity.
source: Both THO and Yra1-C stimulated Sub2's intrinsic ATPase activity.
evidence: This is supported by the ATPase assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Yra1-C stimulated Sub2's intrinsic ATPase activity.
source: Both THO and Yra1-C stimulated Sub2's intrinsic ATPase activity.
evidence: This is supported by the ATPase assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: THO surveys common landmarks in each nuclear mRNP to localize Sub2 for targeted loading of Yra1.
source: We propose that THO surveys common landmarks in each nuclear mRNP to localize Sub2 for targeted loading of Yra1.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: The TREX complex facilitates assembly of export competent mRNPs and functionally connects transcription with nuclear export.
source: The evolutionarily conserved TREX (TRanscription-EXport) complex, which facilitates assembly of export competent mRNPs and functionally connects transcription with nuclear export, is a key player in these events (Masuda et al., 2005; Rehwinkel et al., 2004; Rodríguez-Navarro and Hurt, 2011; Strässer et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The TREX complex in yeast consists of the hetero-pentameric THO complex, the DEAD-box ATPase Sub2 and the mRNA-binding protein Yra1.
source: The TREX complex in yeast consists of the hetero-pentameric THO complex, the DEAD-box ATPase Sub2 and the mRNA-binding protein Yra1 (Chávez et al., 2000; Strässer and Hurt, 2000, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: TREX travels along actively transcribed genes with RNA polymerase II (Pol II).
source: TREX travels along actively transcribed genes with RNA polymerase II (Pol II) (Meinel et al., 2013; Strässer et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: TREX-mediated remodeling yields a targeted deposition of Yra1 on nuclear mRNP.
source: In essence, TREX-mediated remodeling yields a targeted deposition of Yra1 on nuclear mRNP (Abruzzi et al., 2004)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Yra1 serves as a platform to bind hetero-dimeric Mex67•Mtr2.
source: which in turn serves as a platform to bind hetero-dimeric Mex67•Mtr2 (Strässer and Hurt, 2000; Zenklusen et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mex67•Mtr2 is capable of binding to Phe-Gly (FG) repeat regions of nucleoporins.
source: The latter, being capable of binding to Phe-Gly (FG) repeat regions of nucleoporins, provides access to the nuclear pore complex (NPC) (Fribourg et al., 2001; Segref et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mex67 binds via its ubiquitin-associated (UBA) module to the Hpr1 subunit of THO.
source: Although Mex67•Mtr2 is not a bona fide member of the TREX complex, Mex67 binds via its ubiquitin-associated (UBA) module to the Hpr1 subunit of THO (Gwizdek et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Sub2 association with active genes requires an intact THO complex.
source: Previous studies showed that Sub2 association with active genes requires an intact THO complex, and it is thought to be transferred to the mRNA during cotranscriptional mRNP packaging (Abruzzi et al., 2004; Zenklusen et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Sub2 and Mex67•Mtr2 bind to the same regions of Yra1.
source: In addition, Sub2 and Mex67•Mtr2 bind to the same regions of Yra1, suggesting that Sub2 could recruit Yra1 onto mRNP and then be displaced by Mex67•Mtr2 (Strässer and Hurt, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Sub2 could recruit Yra1 onto mRNP and then be displaced by Mex67•Mtr2.
source: In addition, Sub2 and Mex67•Mtr2 bind to the same regions of Yra1, suggesting that Sub2 could recruit Yra1 onto mRNP and then be displaced by Mex67•Mtr2 (Strässer and Hurt, 2001).
evidence: This is a suggestion based on previous findings, representing an inference.

claim: THO is required for the recruitment of Sub2 onto actively transcribed genes.
source: THO is required for the recruitment of Sub2 onto actively transcribed genes (Zenklusen et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: THO exists as a robust structural and functional unit in vivo.
source: Previous studies showed that THO exists as a robust structural and functional unit in vivo, and knockdown of individual subunits causes down-regulation of the other subunits (Huertas et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Knockdown of individual THO subunits causes down-regulation of the other subunits.
source: Previous studies showed that THO exists as a robust structural and functional unit in vivo, and knockdown of individual subunits causes down-regulation of the other subunits (Huertas et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: THO could only be obtained by means of co-expression.
source: Consistent with this, we could only obtain THO by means of co-expression.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observations in the study.

claim: The 360 kDa THO*•Sub2 complex reveals an elongated THO*, ~25 nm from 'head' to 'tail'.
source: The 360 kDa THO*•Sub2 complex reveals an elongated THO*, ~25 nm from 'head' to 'tail' (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by the structural data and Figure 1C.

claim: The dimensions of THO* are close to those reported previously for full-length THO isolated from yeast and analyzed by negative stain EM.
source: Its dimensions are close to those reported previously for full-length THO isolated from yeast and analyzed by negative stain EM (Peña et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison with a previous study.

claim: Tex1 folds into a seven-bladed β-propeller with its smaller top surface facing toward the head.
source: Tex1 folds into a seven-bladed β-propeller with its smaller top surface facing toward the head.
evidence: This is based on the structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: Tex1 is clamped to the base via contacts on two opposite sides of the propeller.
source: It is clamped to the base via contacts on two opposite sides of the propeller.
evidence: This is based on the structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: The N-termini of Tho2 and Hpr1 were localized close to the head.
source: We found that the N-termini of Tho2 and Hpr1 were localized close to the head, while their C-termini were localized at the tail.
evidence: This is based on negative stain EM data with MBP labeling.

claim: The C-termini of Tho2 and Hpr1 were localized at the tail.
source: We found that the N-termini of Tho2 and Hpr1 were localized close to the head, while their C-termini were localized at the tail.
evidence: This is based on negative stain EM data with MBP labeling.

claim: The Tho2 and Hpr1 subunits span the longest dimension of THO*.
source: These data indicate that the Tho2 and Hpr1 subunits span the longest dimension of THO*.
evidence: This is inferred from the EM localization data.

claim: The N-termini of Mft1 and Thp2 were assigned to the head.
source: In addition, the N-termini of Mft1 and Thp2 were assigned to the head, while their C-termini could not be positioned reliably.
evidence: This is based on negative stain EM data with MBP labeling.

claim: The middle region of THO* makes contact with both the Sub2-N and Sub2-C lobes.
source: Interestingly, the middle region of THO* makes contact with both the Sub2-N and Sub2-C lobes and induces a semi-open conformation.
evidence: This is based on the structural data from the THO*•Sub2 crystal structure.

claim: THO* induces a semi-open conformation of Sub2.
source: Interestingly, the middle region of THO* makes contact with both the Sub2-N and Sub2-C lobes and induces a semi-open conformation.
evidence: This is based on the structural data from the THO*•Sub2 crystal structure.

claim: In the absence of nucleotide and RNA, the two RecA domains of DEAD box ATPases are separated, representing an 'open' conformation.
source: DEAD box ATPases like Sub2 exhibit distinct conformations during the ATP hydrolysis cycle. In the absence of nucleotide and RNA, the two RecA domains are separated, representing an 'open' conformation (Caruthers et al., 2000; Shi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: ATP and RNA binding induces a 'closed' form of DEAD box ATPases that is productive for ATP hydrolysis.
source: ATP and RNA binding induces a 'closed' form that is productive for ATP hydrolysis (Sengoku et al., 2006; von Moeller et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The semi-open conformation of Sub2 in the THO*•Sub2 complex is close to its ATP/RNA-bound active state.
source: The semi-open conformation of Sub2 in the THO*•Sub2 complex is close to its ATP/RNA-bound active state (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison with other DEAD-box ATPase structures.

claim: THO* accelerated the ATPase activity of Sub2 by ~3.5-fold.
source: Indeed, we found that THO* accelerated the ATPase activity of Sub2 by ~3.5-fold (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the ATPase assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The Sub2 stimulating activity of THO* is similar to that of full-length THO.
source: The Sub2 stimulating activity of THO* is similar to that of full-length THO, indicating that THO* maintains the full stimulatory effect of THO (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the ATPase assay data comparing THO* and full-length THO.

claim: THO is a previously uncharacterized regulator of the Sub2 ATPase.
source: Collectively, our results demonstrate that THO is a previously uncharacterized regulator of the Sub2 ATPase.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the ATPase assay data.

claim: The ATPase activation mechanism by configuring the two RecA domains in a half-open conformation is shared with several other DEAD-box proteins: Dbp5 in mRNA export, eIF4A in translation initiation, and DDX6 in miRNA-mediated translational repression.
source: Notably, this ATPase activation mechanism by configuring the two RecA domains in a half-open conformation is shared with several other DEAD-box proteins: Dbp5 in mRNA export, eIF4A in translation initiation, and DDX6 in miRNA-mediated translational repression, which are activated by Gle1, eIF4G, and CNOT1, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 3) (Folkmann et al., 2011; Mathys et al., 2014; Montpetit et al., 2011; Schütz et al., 2008).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison and citations to previous studies.

claim: The THO* arrangement of pairs of helices at the THO*-Sub2 interface resembles the MIF4G domains from Gle1, eIF4G, and CNOT1.
source: Moreover, the THO* arrangement of pairs of helices at the THO*-Sub2 interface resembles the MIF4G (middle of eIF4G) domains from Gle1, eIF4G, and CNOT1, further indicating a conserved mechanism of DEAD-box ATPase activation.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison.

claim: Recognition of the C-terminal RecA domain of DEAD-box proteins by their MIF4G containing activators is the primary interaction critical for activation of ATP hydrolysis.
source: Recognition of the C-terminal RecA domain of DEAD-box proteins by their MIF4G containing activators is the primary interaction critical for activation of ATP hydrolysis (Hilbert et al., 2011; Montpetit et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The ATPase activity of a Sub2 E356A/K357A/R358A mutant was no longer activated by THO*.
source: We found that the ATPase activity of a Sub2 E356A/K357A/R358A mutant was no longer activated by THO*, indicating the critical role of the interaction between THO and Sub2-C (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the mutagenesis and ATPase assay data.

claim: D66A and L68D mutants of Sub2 at the THO*-Sub2-N interface compromised the stimulatory effect of THO*.
source: At the Sub2-N lobe, THO* recognizes a groove formed by two helices of Sub2 (Figure 2A). D66A and L68D mutants of Sub2 at this interface compromised the stimulatory effect of THO* (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the mutagenesis and ATPase assay data.

claim: The stimulation of Sub2 ATPase activity by THO requires interactions with both lobes of Sub2.
source: Together, these structure-guided mutagenesis studies demonstrate that the stimulation of Sub2 ATPase activity by THO requires interactions with both lobes of Sub2.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutagenesis data.

claim: The semi-open configuration of Sub2 bound to THO may represent a 'primed' state for efficient mRNP engagement.
source: The semi-open configuration of Sub2 bound to THO may represent a 'primed' state for efficient mRNP engagement.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the structural data.

claim: DEAD-box proteins like Sub2 lack RNA specificity.
source: DEAD-box proteins like Sub2 lack RNA specificity, so they are directed to their physiological RNA substrates by their partners (Linder and Jankowsky, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: THO has been shown to directly bind the phosphorylated C-terminal domain (CTD) of the largest Pol II subunit.
source: THO has recently been shown to directly bind the phosphorylated C-terminal domain (CTD) of the largest Pol II subunit (Meinel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Cotranscriptional loading of Sub2 onto active genes requires the Hpr1 subunit of THO.
source: In addition, cotranscriptional loading of Sub2 onto active genes requires the Hpr1 subunit of THO (Zenklusen et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: THO is well suited to the role of recruiting Sub2 to the transcription machinery, priming and targeting it to appropriate mRNP substrates.
source: Therefore, THO is well suited to the role of recruiting Sub2 to the transcription machinery, priming and targeting it to appropriate mRNP substrates, potentially those that have been properly processed.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: Sub2 has been implicated in loading of Yra1 onto mRNP in an ATP-dependent manner from studies on their human homologs.
source: Sub2 has been implicated in loading of Yra1 onto mRNP in an ATP-dependent manner from studies on their human homologs (Dufu et al., 2010; Luo et al., 2001; Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Yra1 contains two conserved motifs at both termini (N-box and C-box), which are involved in Sub2 binding.
source: Yra1 contains two conserved motifs at both termini (N-box and C-box), which are involved in Sub2 binding (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Yra1 structure.

claim: The two motifs of Yra1 are joined to the central conserved RRM domain through variable regions (N-vr and C-vr), which are implicated in RNA binding.
source: The two motifs of Yra1 are joined to the central conserved RRM domain through variable regions (N-vr and C-vr), which are implicated in RNA binding (Hautbergue et al., 2008; Zenklusen et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The N-box and C-box motifs of Yra1 are functionally redundant.
source: Genetic studies indicated that the N-box and C-box motifs are functionally redundant, but a Yra1 mutant lacking the C-box exhibits a stronger growth phenotype (Zenklusen et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: A Yra1 mutant lacking the C-box exhibits a stronger growth phenotype than one lacking the N-box.
source: Genetic studies indicated that the N-box and C-box motifs are functionally redundant, but a Yra1 mutant lacking the C-box exhibits a stronger growth phenotype (Zenklusen et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Within the Sub2•Yra1-C*•RNA complex, Sub2 adopts a closed conformation with ADP•BeF3 and 6-nt of RNA (U1 to U6) bound in between Sub2-N and Sub2-C.
source: Within this Sub2•Yra1-C*•RNA complex, Sub2 adopts a closed conformation with ADP•BeF3 and 6-nt of RNA (U1 to U6) bound in between Sub2-N and Sub2-C (Figure 3B,C, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on the structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: The RNA is sharply bent between U4 and U5 in the Sub2•Yra1-C*•RNA complex.
source: The RNA is sharply bent between U4 and U5, as observed in structures of other RNA-bound DEAD-box ATPases (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on the structural data and comparison with other structures.

claim: Sub2 is recognized by the conserved C-box of Yra1 (a.a. 208–226), which folds into a helix that fits in the groove formed by two helices of Sub2-N.
source: Sub2 is recognized by the conserved C-box of Yra1 (a.a. 208–226), which folds into a helix that fits in the groove formed by two helices of Sub2-N (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on the structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: Yra1 D216, E218, and Y222 make key polar contacts with Sub2.
source: Specifically, Yra1 D216, E218, and Y222 make key polar contacts with Sub2, whereas L215, M219, and Y222 contribute to van der Waals interactions at the interface.
evidence: This is based on the structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: Yra1 L215, M219, and Y222 contribute to van der Waals interactions at the Sub2-Yra1 interface.
source: Specifically, Yra1 D216, E218, and Y222 make key polar contacts with Sub2, whereas L215, M219, and Y222 contribute to van der Waals interactions at the interface.
evidence: This is based on the structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: Sub2 predominantly interacts with the phosphate-ribose backbone of RNA.
source: Sub2, like other DEAD-box proteins (Linder and Jankowsky, 2011), predominantly interacts with the phosphate-ribose backbone of RNA, with Sub2-N and Sub2-C contacting the 3' and 5' ends, respectively (Figure 3B,C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on the structural data and comparison with other DEAD-box proteins.

claim: Sub2-N and Sub2-C contact the 3' and 5' ends of RNA, respectively.
source: Sub2, like other DEAD-box proteins (Linder and Jankowsky, 2011), predominantly interacts with the phosphate-ribose backbone of RNA, with Sub2-N and Sub2-C contacting the 3' and 5' ends, respectively (Figure 3B,C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on the structural data from the crystal structure.

claim: The RNA binding C-vr region of Yra1 is located close to the RNA in the Sub2•Yra1-C•RNA complex.
source: Notably, the RNA binding C-vr region of Yra1 that precedes C-box is located close to the RNA, which raises the possibility that it could extend the RNA-binding site in the Sub2•Yra1-C•RNA complex.
evidence: This is based on the structural data and inference.

claim: The C-vr region of Yra1 could extend the RNA-binding site in the Sub2•Yra1-C•RNA complex.
source: Notably, the RNA binding C-vr region of Yra1 that precedes C-box is located close to the RNA, which raises the possibility that it could extend the RNA-binding site in the Sub2•Yra1-C•RNA complex.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural data.

claim: Sub2 and RNA formed a complex in the presence of the non-hydrolyzable ATP analogue, ATP-γ-S.
source: Using an electrophoretic mobility shift assay with poly(U) RNA, we found that Sub2 and RNA formed a complex in the presence of the non-hydrolyzable ATP analogue, ATP-γ-S (Figure 4A, compare lanes 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by the EMSA data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Yra1-C is capable of binding RNA.
source: In addition, Yra1-C is capable of binding RNA, while C-box alone is not, indicating that the RNA-binding ability indeed lies in C-vr (Figure 4A, compare lanes 3 and 8).
evidence: This is supported by the EMSA data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: C-box alone is not capable of binding RNA.
source: In addition, Yra1-C is capable of binding RNA, while C-box alone is not, indicating that the RNA-binding ability indeed lies in C-vr (Figure 4A, compare lanes 3 and 8).
evidence: This is supported by the EMSA data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The RNA-binding ability of Yra1 lies in C-vr.
source: In addition, Yra1-C is capable of binding RNA, while C-box alone is not, indicating that the RNA-binding ability indeed lies in C-vr (Figure 4A, compare lanes 3 and 8).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the EMSA data.

claim: The presence of Yra1-C promoted Sub2-RNA interaction, forming a trimeric Sub2•Yra1-C•RNA complex.
source: The presence of Yra1-C promoted Sub2-RNA interaction, forming a trimeric Sub2•Yra1-C•RNA complex (Figure 4A, compare lanes 2 and 4–6).
evidence: This is supported by the EMSA data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The stimulation of RNA binding to Sub2 by Yra1-C was dependent on the presence of both ATP-γ-S and the C-vr region of Yra1.
source: Importantly, this stimulation of RNA binding to Sub2 by Yra1-C was dependent on the presence of both ATP-γ-S and the C-vr region of Yra1 (Figure 4A, compare lanes 6, 7, and 9).
evidence: This is supported by the EMSA data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Sub2 and Yra1-C, by spatially juxtaposing their RNA binding regions, cooperatively bind to RNA.
source: Our structural and biochemical studies suggest that Sub2 and Yra1-C, by spatially juxtaposing their RNA binding regions, cooperatively bind to RNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural and EMSA data.

claim: Human Alyref (Yra1 in yeast) is an activator of the UAP56 (Sub2 in yeast) ATPase.
source: Previous reports showed that human Alyref (Yra1 in yeast) is an activator of the UAP56 (Sub2 in yeast) ATPase (Chang et al., 2013; Taniguchi and Ohno, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Yra1-C is capable of accelerating Sub2 ATPase activity by ~2 fold.
source: We found that Yra1-C is capable of accelerating Sub2 ATPase activity by ~2 fold (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is supported by the ATPase assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The ~2 fold stimulation of Sub2 by Yra1-C is comparable to the reported ~3 fold UAP56 stimulation by full length Alyref.
source: We found that Yra1-C is capable of accelerating Sub2 ATPase activity by ~2 fold (Figure 4B), which is comparable to the reported ~3 fold UAP56 stimulation by full length Alyref.
evidence: This is a comparison with previous findings.

claim: L215D or D216K mutation on Yra1 abolished the stimulatory effect of Yra1-C on Sub2 ATPase activity.
source: L215D or D216K mutation was introduced on Yra1 to, respectively, disrupt the hydrophobic or polar interactions at the Sub2-Yra1 interface (Figure 3D). We found that both mutations abolished the stimulatory effect of Yra1-C (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the mutagenesis and ATPase assay data.

claim: C-box alone, lacking the C-vr RNA binding region, showed no stimulation of Sub2 ATPase activity.
source: Similarly, C-box alone, lacking the C-vr RNA binding region, showed no stimulation of Sub2.
evidence: This is supported by the ATPase assay data.

claim: Yra1-C exhibits a bipartite interaction, with the C-box binding to Sub2-N and the C-vr binding to RNA, both of which contribute to Sub2 activation.
source: Taken together, we conclude that Yra1-C exhibits a bipartite interaction, with the C-box binding to Sub2-N and the C-vr binding to RNA, both of which contribute to Sub2 activation (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: The Sub2 ATPase activity was enhanced by ~4.2 fold in the presence of both THO and Yra1-C.
source: Interestingly, the Sub2 ATPase activity was enhanced by ~4.2 fold, a stronger effect than THO or Yra1-C alone.
evidence: This is supported by the ATPase assay data.

claim: THO and Yra1 act cumulatively to regulate Sub2.
source: Our results suggest that THO and Yra1 act cumulatively to regulate Sub2.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the ATPase assay data.

claim: RNA binding of Sub2 is transient during the ATPase cycle.
source: It should be noted that RNA binding of Sub2 is transient during the ATPase cycle, and could only be detected when turnover of ATP is inhibited.
evidence: This is based on the experimental observations.

claim: The ADP•BeF3-trapped stable trimeric complex of Sub2, Yra1-C, and RNA represents a key snapshot for the ATP-dependent recruitment of Yra1 by Sub2 that occurs on the mRNP.
source: The ADP•BeF3-trapped stable trimeric complex of Sub2, Yra1-C, and RNA, represents a key snapshot for the ATP-dependent recruitment of Yra1 by Sub2 that occurs on the mRNP.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: ATP hydrolysis would trigger release of Sub2 from the mRNP.
source: ATP hydrolysis would then trigger release of Sub2, whose position on the mRNP might be taken by other RNA binding regions (N-vr and RRM) embedded in Yra1.
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: The Sub2 ATP hydrolysis cycle is coupled to loading of Yra1 onto the mRNP.
source: Our studies on the Sub2-Yra1 interaction clearly indicate that the Sub2 ATP hydrolysis cycle is coupled to loading of Yra1 onto the mRNP.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: Some other proteins contain C-box motifs, such as Uif, Chtop, and Luzp4, all of which are capable of binding RNA.
source: Some other proteins have been shown to contain C-box motifs, such as Uif, Chtop, and Luzp4, all of which are capable of binding RNA (Chang et al., 2013; Hautbergue et al., 2009; Viphakone et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Chtop has been reported to stimulate UAP56 ATPase activity.
source: Among them, Chtop has been reported to stimulate UAP56 ATPase activity (Chang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: UAP56 could use the same mechanism to load these factors, in addition to Alyref, onto mRNPs.
source: UAP56 could use the same mechanism to load these factors, in addition to Alyref, onto mRNPs.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: A similar mode of interaction has been reported for the translation initiation factor eIF4A and its activators eIF4B and eIF4H.
source: Like Sub2 and Yra1, a similar mode of interaction has been reported for the translation initiation factor eIF4A and its activators eIF4B and eIF4H (Rozovsky et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: eIF4B and eIF4H bind to the same region of eIF4A, which includes the analogous region of Sub2 recognized by Yra1.
source: eIF4B and eIF4H bind to the same region of eIF4A, which includes the analogous region of Sub2 recognized by Yra1.
evidence: This is based on comparison with previous studies.

claim: eIF4B and eIF4H make additional transient interactions with RNA, and so contribute to RNA affinity of their complexes with eIF4A.
source: Furthermore, eIF4B and eIF4H make additional transient interactions with RNA, and so contribute to RNA affinity of their complexes with eIF4A.
evidence: This is based on previous studies.

claim: The mechanism by which eIF4B and eIF4H stimulate eIF4A could resemble that of Sub2 stimulation by Yra1.
source: The mechanism by which eIF4B and eIF4H stimulate eIF4A could resemble that of Sub2 stimulation by Yra1.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on comparison with the current findings.

claim: C-box containing proteins, together with eIF4B and eIF4H, likely represent a new class of DEAD-box ATPase regulators in addition to the MIF4G domain-containing activators.
source: Thus, C-box containing proteins, together with eIF4B and eIF4H, likely represent a new class of DEAD-box ATPase regulators in addition to the MIF4G domain-containing activators.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: THO mediates targeted deposition of Yra1 and Mex67•Mtr2 on mRNPs through an ATP-dependent process.
source: Here, our structural observations combined with biochemical studies have provided molecular snapshots of these TREX-mediated mRNP remodeling reactions (Figure 5). Our data support a model in which THO mediates targeted deposition of Yra1 and Mex67•Mtr2 on mRNPs through an ATP-dependent process.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: THO binding serves as more than a physical attachment for Sub2.
source: Our studies indicate that THO binding serves as more than a physical attachment.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: In the complex with THO, Sub2 assumes a semi-open conformation, which is similar to its catalytically active state.
source: In the complex with THO, Sub2 assumes a semi-open conformation, which is similar to its catalytically active state.
evidence: This is based on the structural data.

claim: THO, by configuring a semi-open conformation of Sub2, primes it for engaging with mRNA.
source: Our data support a view that THO, by configuring a semi-open conformation of Sub2, primes it for engaging with mRNA.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: The mechanism that restricts the activity of TREX to properly processed transcripts is currently not clear.
source: The mechanism that restricts the activity of TREX to properly processed transcripts is currently not clear.
evidence: This acknowledges a gap in current understanding.

claim: THO could deposit Sub2 upon recognizing a certain feature of an mRNP.
source: Potentially, THO could deposit Sub2 upon recognizing a certain feature of an mRNP.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis.

claim: TREX functions genome-wide, for both intronless and intron-containing genes.
source: Previous studies have shown that TREX functions genome-wide, for both intronless and intron-containing genes (Abruzzi et al., 2004; Lei et al., 2011; Masuda et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The ATP-dependent binding of Sub2 to an mRNP is coupled to Yra1 loading.
source: Our biochemical and structural analyses revealed the presence of a stable Sub2•Yra1-C•RNA complex, suggesting that the ATP-dependent binding of Sub2 to an mRNP is coupled to Yra1 loading.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural and biochemical data.

claim: THO and Yra1 could act together to load Sub2 and Yra1 onto the mRNP.
source: Since THO and Yra1 cumulatively stimulated Sub2 ATPase activity in vitro (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C), THO and Yra1 could act together to load Sub2 and Yra1 onto the mRNP.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the biochemical data.

claim: THO likely stays on site as it assists in loading of Mex67•Mtr2 in subsequent remodeling reactions.
source: THO likely stays on site as it assists in loading of Mex67•Mtr2 in subsequent remodeling reactions (see discussion below).
evidence: This is a speculative inference.

claim: TREX function is connected to pre-mRNA 3'-end processing through the interaction between Yra1 and Pcf11.
source: Previous studies indicated that TREX function is connected to pre-mRNA 3'-end processing through the interaction between Yra1 and Pcf11, the Pol II CTD binding subunit of cleavage-polyadenylation factor CF1A (Johnson et al., 2009, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Yra1 is recruited to the transcription machinery by Pcf11, and then undergoes a concerted deposition with Sub2 onto the mRNP.
source: It has been suggested that Yra1 is recruited to the transcription machinery by Pcf11, and then undergoes a concerted deposition with Sub2 onto the mRNP.
evidence: This is a suggestion from previous studies.

claim: The C-box of Yra1 has been found in other mRNA binding proteins, including Uif, Chtop, and Luzp4, all of which interact with the UAP56 ATPase, RNA, and the export receptor TAP•p15 (Mex67•Mtr2 in yeast).
source: It should also be noted that the C-box of Yra1, which mediates Sub2 binding, has been found in other mRNA binding proteins, including Uif, Chtop, and Luzp4, all of which interact with the UAP56 ATPase, RNA, and the export receptor TAP•p15 (Mex67•Mtr2 in yeast) (Chang et al., 2013; Hautbergue et al., 2009; Viphakone et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: ATP-dependent deposition of export factors on mRNPs is likely a conserved mechanism for C-box containing proteins in higher eukaryotes.
source: Hence, ATP-dependent deposition of export factors on mRNPs is likely a conserved mechanism for C-box containing proteins in higher eukaryotes.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the current findings and previous studies.

claim: Binding of Mex67•Mtr2 and Sub2 to Yra1 is mutually exclusive.
source: Because binding of Mex67•Mtr2 and Sub2 to Yra1 is mutually exclusive, recruitment of Mex67•Mtr2 is thought to drive the dissociation of Sub2 from the mRNP (Strässer and Hurt, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Recruitment of Mex67•Mtr2 is thought to drive the dissociation of Sub2 from the mRNP.
source: Because binding of Mex67•Mtr2 and Sub2 to Yra1 is mutually exclusive, recruitment of Mex67•Mtr2 is thought to drive the dissociation of Sub2 from the mRNP (Strässer and Hurt, 2001).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on previous findings.

claim: THO is also implicated in Mex67•Mtr2 loading via the Hpr1 subunit.
source: In addition, THO is also implicated in Mex67•Mtr2 loading via the Hpr1 subunit (Gwizdek et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Both Alyref and Thoc5 (a subunit of human THO) make contacts with TAP•p15, and promote RNA binding to TAP•p15.
source: Consistently, studies on the human TREX complex showed that both Alyref and Thoc5 (a subunit of human THO) make contacts with TAP•p15, and promote RNA binding to TAP•p15 (Viphakone et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: TREX functions as a recruitment platform to bring export factors in spatial proximity to nascent transcripts, and coordinates multiple steps of mRNP assembly.
source: Therefore, TREX functions as a recruitment platform to bring export factors in spatial proximity to nascent transcripts, and coordinates multiple steps of mRNP assembly.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the current findings and previous studies.
